### Problem: Design Browser History {#sec-ds-p2-history}

::: {.p-statement}
Simulate one browser tab. `BrowserHistory(homepage)` starts on `homepage`; then:

- `visit(url)` — go to `url` from the current page, **erasing all forward history**;
- `back(steps)` — move back up to `steps` pages (stop at the first page) and return the page you land on;
- `forward(steps)` — move forward up to `steps` pages (stop at the newest page) and return the page you land on.

URLs have at most $20$ characters, $1 \le$ `steps` $\le 100$, and there are at most $5000$ calls. The sample visits `google, facebook, youtube` from `leetcode`, then `back(1) = facebook`, `back(1) = google`, `forward(1) = facebook`, `visit(linkedin)`, `forward(2) = linkedin`, `back(2) = google`, `back(7) = leetcode`.

Source: [LC 1472 · Design Browser History](https://leetcode.com/problems/design-browser-history/){.solved difficulty="Medium"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
The history is a list of versions of "where the tab is", and a cursor says which version is current. `back` and `forward` only move the cursor, clamped to the list. `visit` discards every version after the cursor and appends the new page. The discarded suffix need not even be deleted: an `end` marker that says where the live history stops makes `visit` $O(1)$ and leaves stale pages beyond `end`, unreachable.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
1. **One list, one cursor.** `visit` deletes `hist[i+1:]` and appends; `back`/`forward` clamp the cursor. $O(1)$ navigation; `visit` costs $O(\text{dropped} + 1)$, which is $O(1)$ amortised because each page is dropped at most once. This class is the model for the stress tests.
2. **Two stacks.** `left` holds the past and the present (top = current page), `right` holds the forward pages. `back` moves pages from `left` to `right` one at a time, `forward` moves them back, `visit` clears `right`. $O(\text{steps})$ per move.
3. **Array with an end marker.** Keep the cursor and an `end` index one past the newest live page. `visit` writes at `cur + 1` (appending only when the array is full) and sets `end = cur + 2`; nothing is ever deleted. Every operation is $O(1)$ amortised.

**Operation contract (final form).** Invariant **I**: `arr[0..end-1]` is the live history, oldest first, and $0 \le$ `cur` $<$ `end` $\le$ `len(arr)`. Entries at index $\ge$ `end` are garbage.

| Operation | What it does | How **I** survives | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| `visit(url)` | `cur += 1`; write `url` at `cur` (append if `cur == len(arr)`); `end = cur + 1` | the live history is the old prefix up to the cursor plus the new page | $O(1)$ amortised |
| `back(k)` | `cur = max(0, cur - k)` | the clamp keeps `cur` $\ge 0$ | $O(1)$ |
| `forward(k)` | `cur = min(end - 1, cur + k)` | the clamp keeps `cur` $<$ `end` | $O(1)$ |
:::

The buttons are in order. Each one keeps the previous solution and changes only what that form changes.

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### One list, one cursor

::: {.form-next}
The definition in a few lines: navigation clamps `i`; `visit` cuts everything after `i` and appends. This is the version to explain first in an interview.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("history", "cursor")
    assert str(final) == ("outputs leetcode google facebook youtube facebook google "
                          "facebook linkedin linkedin google leetcode")
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
class BrowserHistoryList:
    def __init__(self, homepage):
        self.hist = [homepage]
        self.i = 0

    def visit(self, url):
        del self.hist[self.i + 1:]
        self.hist.append(url)
        self.i = len(self.hist) - 1

    def back(self, steps):
        self.i = max(0, self.i - steps)
        return self.hist[self.i]

    def forward(self, steps):
        self.i = min(len(self.hist) - 1, self.i + steps)
        return self.hist[self.i]


SAMPLE = [("visit", "google"), ("visit", "facebook"), ("visit", "youtube"), ("back", 1),
          ("back", 1), ("forward", 1), ("visit", "linkedin"), ("forward", 2), ("back", 2),
          ("back", 7)]
SAMPLE_OUT = [None, None, None, "facebook", "google", "facebook", None, "linkedin",
              "google", "leetcode"]


def replay(b, ops):
    return [getattr(b, name)(arg) for name, arg in ops]


assert replay(BrowserHistoryList("leetcode"), SAMPLE) == SAMPLE_OUT
```

##### C++

```cpp
class BrowserHistoryList {
    vector<string> hist;
    int i = 0;
 public:
    BrowserHistoryList(string homepage) { hist.push_back(homepage); }
    void visit(string url) {
        hist.erase(hist.begin() + i + 1, hist.end());
        hist.push_back(url); i = (int)hist.size() - 1;
    }
    string back(int steps) { i = max(0, i - steps); return hist[i]; }
    string forward(int steps) { i = min((int)hist.size() - 1, i + steps); return hist[i]; }
};
```
:::

#### Two stacks

::: {.form-next}
The classic interview alternative. `left` holds the past and present (top = current), `right` the forward branch (top = next page). `back` moves one page at a time from `left` to `right`, `forward` moves them back, and `visit` empties `right`. No index arithmetic, but a move costs $O(\text{steps})$ instead of $O(1)$.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("history", "stack")
    assert str(final) == ("outputs leetcode google facebook youtube facebook google "
                          "facebook linkedin linkedin google leetcode")
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
class BrowserStacks:
    def __init__(self, homepage):
        self.left = [homepage]      # past + present, top = current
        self.right = []             # forward branch, top = next

    def visit(self, url):
        self.right.clear()
        self.left.append(url)

    def back(self, steps):
        for _ in range(min(steps, len(self.left) - 1)):
            self.right.append(self.left.pop())
        return self.left[-1]

    def forward(self, steps):
        for _ in range(min(steps, len(self.right))):
            self.left.append(self.right.pop())
        return self.left[-1]


assert replay(BrowserStacks("leetcode"), SAMPLE) == SAMPLE_OUT
```

##### C++

```cpp
class BrowserStacks {
    vector<string> left, right;
 public:
    BrowserStacks(string homepage) { left.push_back(homepage); }
    void visit(string url) { right.clear(); left.push_back(url); }
    string back(int steps) {
        for (int k = 0; k < steps && left.size() > 1; ++k) {
            right.push_back(left.back()); left.pop_back();
        }
        return left.back();
    }
    string forward(int steps) {
        for (int k = 0; k < steps && !right.empty(); ++k) {
            left.push_back(right.back()); right.pop_back();
        }
        return left.back();
    }
};
```
:::

#### Array with an end marker

::: {.form-next}
Back to one array, but `visit` no longer deletes anything: it overwrites slot `cur + 1` (growing the array only when it is full) and moves `end`. Stale pages beyond `end` stay in memory and are never read. All three operations are $O(1)$ amortised. The stress test replays random operations against the list model and also checks the invariant.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("history", "window")
    assert str(final) == ("outputs leetcode google facebook youtube facebook google "
                          "facebook linkedin linkedin google leetcode")
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
class BrowserHistory:
    def __init__(self, homepage):
        self.arr = [homepage]
        self.cur = 0
        self.end = 1                # arr[0..end-1] is the live history

    def visit(self, url):
        self.cur += 1
        if self.cur == len(self.arr):
            self.arr.append(url)    # amortised O(1) growth
        else:
            self.arr[self.cur] = url
        self.end = self.cur + 1     # everything after the cursor is now garbage

    def back(self, steps):
        self.cur = max(0, self.cur - steps)
        return self.arr[self.cur]

    def forward(self, steps):
        self.cur = min(self.end - 1, self.cur + steps)
        return self.arr[self.cur]


assert replay(BrowserHistory("leetcode"), SAMPLE) == SAMPLE_OUT
# stress: random operations against the list model (and the stacks), invariant after each
for _ in range(300):
    model, stk, fast = BrowserHistoryList("h"), BrowserStacks("h"), BrowserHistory("h")
    for _ in range(40):
        r = random.random()
        if r < 0.4:
            u = f"p{random.randint(0, 5)}"
            model.visit(u); stk.visit(u); fast.visit(u)
        else:
            name, k = ("back" if r < 0.7 else "forward"), random.randint(1, 4)
            want = getattr(model, name)(k)
            assert getattr(stk, name)(k) == want == getattr(fast, name)(k)
        assert 0 <= fast.cur < fast.end <= len(fast.arr)
        assert fast.arr[:fast.end] == model.hist
```

##### C++

```cpp
class BrowserHistory {
    vector<string> arr;
    int cur = 0, end = 1;          // arr[0..end-1] is the live history
 public:
    BrowserHistory(string homepage) { arr.push_back(homepage); }
    void visit(string url) {
        ++cur;
        if (cur == (int)arr.size()) arr.push_back(url); else arr[cur] = url;
        end = cur + 1;
    }
    string back(int steps) { cur = max(0, cur - steps); return arr[cur]; }
    string forward(int steps) { cur = min(end - 1, cur + steps); return arr[cur]; }
};
```
:::

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**One list, one cursor:** $O(1)$ `back`/`forward`; `visit` deletes the dropped suffix, $O(1)$ amortised over the whole run because every page is dropped at most once. **Two stacks:** $O(1)$ amortised `visit` (clearing `right` is paid for by the pushes that filled it), $O(\min(\text{steps}, \text{history}))$ per `back`/`forward`, at most $100$ moves here. **Array with an end marker:** $O(1)$ amortised for all three. Space is $O(\text{pages visited})$ for every form; the end-marker form may keep up to that many stale pages.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- **`back` past the homepage** and **`forward` past the newest page** are clamped, not errors.
- **`visit` must kill the forward branch**: after `visit(linkedin)`, `forward` can never reach `youtube` again. Forgetting the truncation (the `del`, the `end` update, or `right.clear()`) is the most common wrong answer.
- **`forward` with no future**: `end - 1 == cur`, so the current page is returned unchanged.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistakes"}
- **A fixed-size array.** Sizing the array for "a few visits" overflows at $5000$ visits; either grow it like a vector or size it by the call limit.
- **Advancing the cursor without clamping**: `min`/`max` are what make an oversized `steps` legal.
- **Popping the homepage** in the two-stack form: guard with `len(left) > 1`.
:::

**Variants.** Undo/redo in an editor is the same structure: a list of states, a cursor, and "a new edit discards the redo branch". Keeping the branches instead turns the list into a tree of versions with a parent pointer per node.

::: {.practice}
- [LC 2296 · Design a Text Editor](https://leetcode.com/problems/design-a-text-editor/){difficulty="Hard"} — a cursor that moves left and right over text: the two-stack form, with characters instead of pages.
:::
